claim: FRESCO is an in-house developed method for framework for rapid enzyme stabilization by computational libraries.
source: This computational protocol incorporates two algorithms to calculate folding free energy (ΔGFold, expressed in kJ mol−1), and compares these calculations (ΔΔGFold) between the wild-type structure and variants with a single mutation.

claim: FRESCO incorporates two algorithms to calculate folding free energy (ΔGFold).
source: This computational protocol incorporates two algorithms to calculate folding free energy (ΔGFold, expressed in kJ mol−1), and compares these calculations (ΔΔGFold) between the wild-type structure and variants with a single mutation.
evidence: Description of the FRESCO computational approach

source: Of the 177 selected mutations, 25 mutations brought about a significant increase in apparent melting temperature (ΔTm ≥ +3 °C).

source: Of the 151 mutants for which a melting temperature could be measured, 52 had a similar Tm when compared to wild-type ADHA (−1 ≤ ΔTm ≤ +1 °C), 43 were destabilizing (ΔTm < −1 °C), and 56 were stabilizing (ΔTm > +1 °C) (Figure 2).

claim: 56 mutants were stabilizing (ΔTm > +1 °C).
source: Of the 151 mutants for which a melting temperature could be measured, 52 had a similar Tm when compared to wild-type ADHA (−1 ≤ ΔTm ≤ +1 °C), 43 were destabilizing (ΔTm < −1 °C), and 56 were stabilizing (ΔTm > +1 °C) (Figure 2).

claim: Enzymes that can be easily degraded after some time enable greater metabolic adaptability for the organism.
source: Moreover, enzymes that can be easily degraded after some time enable greater metabolic adaptability for the organism, for instance when a local resource depletes, or a signaling event occurs (DePristo et al., 2005; Parsell and Sauer, 1989).

claim: Improved side-chain packing and hydrophobic interactions are the likely source of the stabilizing effect of mutations G149A, L150F, V193L, T194V, and V217P.
source: G149A, L150F (the most stabilizing mutation of all), V193L, T194V, and V217P all contributed substantially to thermostability, with up to 14 °C increase in the Tm values at the single mutant level (Table 2). The structural analysis clearly shows that improved side-chain packing and hydrophobic interactions are the likely source of their stabilizing effect.
evidence: Structural analysis and inference from crystal structure data

claim: V238L promotes more extended interaction of the subunits within the tetramer by allowing a hydrophobic interaction with itself at the dimer interface.
source: V238L (+7 °C) is a unique case, promoting more extended interaction of the subunits within the tetramer (Figure 5). Curiously, the mutation does so by allowing a hydrophobic interaction with itself at the dimer interface.

claim: The large (+8 °C) stability effect of M157K very likely arises from the removal of a solvent-exposed hydrophobic group and its replacement with the charged and hydrophilic amine of a lysine residue.
source: Among the identified mutations, M157K is the only one that replaces a hydrophobic residue with a hydrophilic and charged side chain (Figure 4C). It has a large (+8 °C; Table 2) effect on protein stability, which very likely arises from the removal of a solvent-exposed hydrophobic group and its replacement with the charged and hydrophilic amine of a lysine residue.
evidence: Structural analysis and inference from mutation characteristics

claim: The conspicuous (+5 °C) stability of N212R can be tentatively attributed to the more pronounced polarity of an arginine side chain as compared to an asparagine.
source: Lastly, N212R is possibly the most puzzling mutation. It positions an arginine side chain in a fully solvent-exposed location (Figure 4C) and its conspicuous (+5 °C) stability can be tentatively attributed to the more pronounced polarity of an arginine side chain as compared to an asparagine (Szilágyi and Závodszky, 2000).
evidence: Structural analysis and inference supported by citation to Szilágyi and Závodszky, 2000

claim: All stabilizing mutations of M9 promote hydrophobic packing of side chains or install highly polar and charged groups on fully solvent-exposed positions on the protein surface.
source: In summary, the detailed structural analysis of the mutation sites reveals a consistent pattern concerning the stabilizing effects: all stabilizing mutations of M9 promote hydrophobic packing of side chains or install highly polar and charged groups on fully solvent-exposed positions on the protein surface.

claim: Prolines often occur at 'helical capping' positions by restraining the backbone conformation and positioning a substituted backbone amino group that is unable to form H-bonding interactions.
source: Prolines often occur at 'helical capping' positions by restraining the backbone conformation and positioning a substituted backbone amino group that is unable to form H-bonding interactions (Richardson and Richardson, 1988).
evidence: Supported by citation to Richardson and Richardson, 1988

claim: The V217P mutation follows the trend of prolines occurring at helical capping positions.
source: V217P is a seemingly conservative mutation at the beginning of an α-helix and yet caused a significant effect (+3 °C; Table 2 and Figure 4C). Prolines often occur at 'helical capping' positions by restraining the backbone conformation and positioning a substituted backbone amino group that is unable to form H-bonding interactions (Richardson and Richardson, 1988). The V217P mutation follows this trend.
evidence: Structural analysis and inference from known proline behavior

claim: Dimers and tetramers may gain a lot of stability from having subunit-subunit interfaces that stabilize hydrophobic regions of the enzyme.
source: Dimers and tetramers may gain a lot of stability from having subunit-subunit interfaces that stabilize hydrophobic regions of the enzyme.
